slot.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated particles
slot.brief: Compare de Broglie wavelengths of an electron and a proton accelerated through the same potential difference.

stem: An electron and a proton, initially at rest, each gain the same kinetic energy in an accelerator. If $m_p/m_e=1840$, what is the ratio of the proton’s de Broglie wavelength to the electron’s?

verdicts.working: For equal kinetic energy in the nonrelativistic regime, p = √(2mK) and λ = h/p. Hence λₚ/λₑ = √(mₑ/mₚ) = 1/√1840.
issues: The nonrelativistic assumption is unstated; at relativistic kinetic energies the wavelength ratio depends on the energy.

working:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$ for kinetic energy $K$.\\
$\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_eK_e}{m_pK_p}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_e}{m_p}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1840}}$.

Independent check: For equal kinetic energy in the nonrelativistic regime, p = √(2mK) and λ = h/p. Hence λₚ/λₑ = √(mₑ/mₚ) = 1/√1840.
solution:
For a particle with kinetic energy $K$, $4\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$.
Since $K_p=K_e$,
$$\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_e}{m_p}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1840}}.$$
